statusMeaning.port: Required change; implemented with authored tests in the phase the row names, before the release the row names.
statusMeaning.already-ported: PiSharp already has the behaviour; the evidence field cites the file.
statusMeaning.no-op: Nothing to change in PiSharp; the evidence field says why.
statusMeaning.ported: Ported in this sync; the evidence field lists the commits and the authored tests, each test as `<file>: <case id>`.
statusMeaning.ported-with-deferral: Ported except for what the deferred field names, with the reason; the evidence field is as for ported.

notesMeaning: A row's notes are planning notes written before its port and describe the code as it was then.
pulledInByMeaning: A row with pulledInBy takes the earliest phase of the rows it names, which cannot be ported without it, and that phase's release.

releaseMeaning.1.5.0.x: Follows as an experimental 1.5.0.x patch (phases 5 to 7), per the release cut decision 0013 records.

changelogBullets: Bullet ids are <package>@<version>/<section>#<n>: the top-level bullets numbered in order under each section of ## [1.3.0], ## [1.4.0] and ## [1.5.0] of packages/<package>/CHANGELOG.md at v1.5.0. The coding-agent changelog repeats user-visible ai and tui bullets, and "New Features" bullets summarise Added and Breaking bullets; a repeated bullet maps to the rows of the bullet it repeats (repeatedBullets). Rows with an empty changelog cover changes no bullet names.

rows.change: resolveTranscriptTools() takes a TranscriptToolSupport ("none", "additions" or "changes") and returns foldedSystemMessages instead of anchorsAdditions. Responses models with mid-conversation system messages and additional_tools ("changes") send no top-level tools and declare every tool in additional_tools items starting at the head of the input; each later item follows an incremental-tools notice that restates tools still unavailable, and true removals are announced in the system update text. Tool search and Kimi tool messages ("additions") fold the top-level list up to the last removal or redeclaration and keep later additions anchored, so the cached prefix changes once per removal instead of on every later load.
rows.notes: Completions: PiSharp anchors Kimi tool messages only while no tool was ever removed (CompletionsToolDeclarationProjector.CanAnchorAdditions, CompletionsToolDeclarationProjector.cs:161, used at CompletionsTranscriptProjector.cs:75-93); port the fold up to the last non-additive change. Responses, Codex and Azure: PiSharp never implemented additional_tools or tool search and always sends the current tool list (docs/compatibility/responses-tools-sdk-reference.md; Azure refuses those compat flags at AzureResponsesRequestFactory.cs:52). The "changes" and "additions" modes there are new request shapes for catalog models flagged supportsAdditionalTools or supportsToolSearch (openai.json, openai-codex.json, github-copilot.json), so they need their own wire tests.
rows.deferred: Responses/Codex/Azure additional_tools ("changes") and tool search ("additions") are request shapes PiSharp never implemented; AzureResponsesRequestFactory refuses those flags. Removal announcements belong to that mode.

rows.notes: PiSharp tests the text length at CompletionsTranscriptProjector.cs:178, ResponsesTranscriptProjector.cs:488 and :492, and GoogleRequestProjector.cs:292. Use JavaScript trim() semantics (its whitespace and line-terminator set), not char.IsWhiteSpace. Mistral (MistralTools.cs:156) is unchanged upstream.

rows.change: validateToolArguments() parses a structuredClone of the arguments with one cached pi-schema validator per schema: compile(schema, { formats, coerce: true, unresolvedRefs: "reject" }).parse(). Every schema gets the same coercion whether TypeBox, pi-schema or plain JSON built it (MCP tools gain TypeBox's conversions), and TypeBox-only features (Refine, BigInt/Undefined/Void, codecs, Format.Set, regex property names) no longer apply. The error keeps its frame (`Validation failed for tool "<name>":`, `  - <path>: <message>` lines, `Received arguments:`) with pi-schema's messages and dotted paths from JSON Pointers (`edits.0.oldText: missing`, `root`).
rows.notes: PiSharp validates with its TypeBox 1.3.27 port (ToolArgumentValidation.cs ValidateCore: normalizeOptionalNulls, Value.Convert by ToolSchemaOrigin, Compile, coerceWithJsonSchema), called from ToolInvoker.cs:350. Switch the tool path to schema.compile-validator, schema.coercion, schema.formats and schema.unresolved-refs. ToolSchemaOrigin then no longer changes the result: keep it for API compatibility or obsolete it, and update api.md's ParametersOrigin row and PiNodeOwner's parametersOrigin mapping. Keep the TypeBox engine itself: TypeBoxJsonSchema (config files) uses its Validator. Expected error texts in tests change. The durable copy (src/PiSharp.Durable/Internal/PiAi/Validation.cs) moves in phase 4. The argumentsError check at the top of 1.5.0's validateToolArguments comes from 87f9a3641 (another group's row). Decision 0013 'Tool argument validation': native C# tools keep their JSON Schema parameters.

rows.change: StreamingJsonParser reads each piece of JSON text once (linear time), never throws, and returns snapshots that never change once returned and share finished containers; append() also returns JsonChange operations (set at a path, append to a string). ToolCallArgumentsStream (append, replace for providers that resend the whole text, finish for one final parse) replaces re-running parseStreamingJson on the accumulated text in every provider. Partial values differ slightly from parseStreamingJson: trailing whitespace in an open string is kept, strings with raw control characters or invalid escapes stay visible, and NaN/Infinity words are dropped.
rows.notes: PiSharp's providers call StreamingJson.Parse (the parseStreamingJson port) on the whole accumulated text per delta (for example BedrockEventState.cs:181, OpenAICompletionsWireSource.cs:454, PiMessagesEventMapper.cs:88), the quadratic cost upstream removed. Port the parser and ToolCallArgumentsStream as new [Experimental] API and switch each provider (Google is not on upstream's list). This row is the parser; D1 owns the fixes built on it: ai@1.5.0/Fixed#3 and coding-agent@1.5.0/Fixed#17 (CPU and memory), agent@1.5.0/Fixed#1 (proxy), and the rendering half of New Features#2 (tui@1.5.0/Fixed#9, coding-agent@1.5.0/Fixed#31). finish() uses parseToolCallArguments with argumentsError (87f9a3641, another group). packages/ai/test/streaming-json.test.ts and test/data/json-test-suite.json give authored cases. Decision 0013 design point 'StreamingJsonParser'.

rows.change: pi.exec() accepts ExecOptions.maxBuffer, a byte limit on stdout and stderr combined (default the smaller of 256 MiB and the runtime string limit; an invalid value rejects before spawning). New C# members carry [Experimental].
rows.deferred: Native pi.exec still captures at most 1 MiB per pipe (the separated process runner's per-pipe bound), so native output stops and reads truncated at 1 MiB per pipe even when maxBuffer (default 256 MiB) is larger. The bridge honours maxBuffer in full.

rows.change: After SIGTERM, exec escalates to SIGKILL when the child still has neither an exit code nor a signal code; the old check !proc.killed was always false once SIGTERM had been sent, so a child that ignored SIGTERM was never killed (c466a3595).

The native path (NativeExtensionExecHost through NativeProcessRunner) needs checking that a cancelled or timed-out child that ignores SIGTERM is killed. Pairs with group C's core.exec-max-buffer, which also ends the process.

rows.change: SessionManager._appendEntry remembers the previous leaf and, if _persist throws (ENOSPC, EBUSY, ETIMEDOUT), pops the entry from fileEntries, removes it from byId, restores the leaf and rethrows. An entry that was not written never becomes the parent of later entries, so a resumed session keeps its history, including the first system message that declares the tools.
rows.notes: Native sessions already behave this way: SessionLogStore.AppendAsync builds the next snapshot aside (SessionLogStore.cs:196-200) and CommitBytesAsync publishes it only after write, flush and checkpoint succeed (SessionLogStore.cs:219). A failure poisons the store (SessionLogStore.cs:222), so later appends are refused (SessionLogStore.cs:174) instead of chaining to an unwritten parent. PersistentAgentSession records the fault (for example PersistentAgentSession.Activation.cs:178). That is stricter than upstream, which keeps writing after the failure, and the difference is pre-existing. The port is the bridge's fallback copy of SessionManager (session-manager.mjs:722-727, used when the Pi npm packages are not installed), which still keeps the entry in memory. 0013 lists session write failures under the core area. Move with core.fork-single-file-handle and the projectContextEntry export of core.branch-summary-context-edits, which touch the same module.
rows.deferred: Only the Node bridge's fallback SessionManager copy follows v1.5.0. Native sessions already keep memory in line with the file (the snapshot is published only after a write succeeds), but after a write that may have reached the file the session faults and accepts no more writes, where upstream rolls the entry back and keeps writing. Whether native sessions follow upstream there is an owner decision (a possibly torn line stays in the file).

rows.change: execCommand (pi.exec) decodes stdout and stderr with one StringDecoder("utf8") per stream instead of data.toString() per chunk. It flushes each decoder with end() on both completion paths, so a multi-byte character split across chunks is no longer corrupted.
rows.notes: Native pi.exec already decodes correctly: SeparatedProcessCapture buffers each pipe's bytes and decodes the whole buffer once (SeparatedProcessCapture.cs:26-35), and NativeExtensionExecHost returns those strings. The Node bridge's own execCommand, which TS extensions' pi.exec always uses, still calls data.toString() per chunk (runtime.mjs:51-52). Port it together with D1's pi.exec limits (coding-agent@1.5.0/Fixed#7 and #8, coding-agent@1.5.0/Added#2 maxBuffer and truncated) and core.exec-spawn-error-stderr, which rewrite the same function. 0013 lists the pi.exec() limits under the core area.

rows.change: When the child process fails (for example a missing executable raises a spawn error), execCommand still resolves with code 1, but stderr is now the collected stderr or, if that is empty, the error's message, instead of an empty string.
rows.notes: The bridge execCommand resolves an empty stderr both for a synchronous spawn throw (runtime.mjs:43) and for the 'error' event (runtime.mjs:58, done(1)); use stderr || error.message in both. Native pi.exec throws an IOException when a run fails to start (NativeExtensionExecHost.cs:127-129). Under the standing rule (PiSharp follows what current Pi does), a process that could not start resolves to Pi's { stderr: <message>, code: 1 } result. Port with core.exec-utf8-chunk-decoding.

rows.change: resolvePackageSources catches a failed install of a configured or -e package and skips it, as offline mode does. It returns PackageInstallFailure { source, scope, message } in ResolvedPaths.installFailures. The resource loader turns each failure into an extension warning: Extension package "<source>": failed to install (<message>). Run "pi remove <source>[ --local]" to remove it from settings.json. For -e sources it says "Check the source and try again." --help, --list-models and pi config now print runtime diagnostics, so the warning shows there too. pi install and pi update --extensions still exit non-zero, and the install is retried on the next start or /reload.
rows.notes: PiPackageManager's InstallMissing lets InstallParsedSource throw (PiPackageManager.cs:389-399), so a configured package that cannot install aborts resolution. PiResolvedPaths has no failure list (PiPackageSource.cs:63). --help and --list-models report only the startup settings diagnostics (PiCommand.cs:171-188). The config command resolves both scopes (PiPackageCommands.cs:276-278) without printing install warnings. Port the failure record, the warning text with scope-specific hints, its merge into the extension run's diagnostics (PiExtensionRun.cs:71-73, also on /reload), the earlier runtime-diagnostics report and the pi config warnings. Add upstream's packages.md paragraph to the website page. Tests use the fake package process runner; no network.

A failed attempt hidden after a successful retry, or replaced content, therefore no longer reaches the /tree summary, matching live context and compaction; tool results are still skipped.

(SessionBranchSummaryPlanner.cs:61). ProjectEntry already takes a replacement and returns nothing for a null one (SessionContextInfluenceProjector.cs:43-46). Collect the latest context_edit per targetId from the entries passed in and pass its replacement. Both callers benefit (PersistentAgentSession.NavigationSummary.cs:30, PersistentAgentSession.Compaction.cs:270). In the bridge fallback, export projectContextEntry (session-manager.mjs:223) and apply it in branch-summarization.mjs (getMessageFromEntry :37, prepareBranchEntries :56). Its self-update target always reports that this installation cannot update itself (src/PiSharp.Cli/Packages/PiPackageCommands.cs:408-414), so there is no marker to parse.

rows.change: The package manifest gains pi.changelogPath (package-relative, resolved safely, else CHANGELOG.md in the package root), carried through PathMetadata/SourceInfo. On a fresh interactive launch pi compares each package's installed version with extensionChangelogVersions[key] in global settings, shows the newer entries under "Extension Updates" (one line per package with collapseChangelog), and records the version; a package seen for the first time is recorded without a notice.

PiSharp shows its own changelog the same way (InteractiveMode.cs:522-540 GetChangelogForDisplay with lastChangelogVersion; collapseChangelog in InteractiveSettings.cs), so reuse that parser. Applies to the npm and git packages PiPackageManager installs; decide what native extension packages report. settings.schema.json gains extensionChangelogVersions (refresh it with the other settings-schema rows).

rows.change: pi update can run a user-configured self-update command: PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND (split on whitespace, no quoting) or else the selfUpdateCommand argv setting, read from global settings only. It runs only when the release check reports a newer version (or with --force), with {packageName}, {version} and {installSpec} filled from that release, and replaces install-method detection; afterwards pi checks the installed version (its package.json, or `pi --version` on PATH) and warns when it did not change. The "cannot self-update" message names both options.

The command comes from the environment or global settings only, never a project file; spawn it without a shell. PiCommand.cs carries the --help environment list.

rows.change: main() wraps its first process.cwd() call: on ENOENT it prints, in red, "Error: The current working directory no longer exists. rows.change: Aborts, timeouts and close() now request worker termination and settle the result right away instead of awaiting the worker's exit, which on Bun could hang while a non-interruptible built-in ran. Hosts that need actual exit use onWorkerStarted(exited) or acquireWorker()'s release callback.
rows.notes: PiSharp runs scripts in Jint in a child process or thread (decision 0003); on abort or timeout it waits for TerminateAsync up to TerminationLimit 10 s (CodemodeSandbox.cs:169, :444-448) before settling, and CloseAsync (:158-163) and RetireAsync (CodemodeWorkers.cs:164-178) also wait for exit. Settling on the request changes the public contract for embedders; record it in codemode-engine.md. Exit tracking moves to codemode.worker-lifetime-hooks.

rows.change: CodemodeSandbox options gain acquireWorker(), a synchronous hook that reserves shared capacity before a worker starts and returns a release callback run on actual worker exit or constructor failure, and onWorkerStarted(exited), which hands the host a promise that resolves when the worker really exits, independent of the script result.
rows.notes: CodemodeSandboxOptions (CodemodeTypes.cs:140-163) has no capacity or start hooks. New public API needs [Experimental] like the rest of PiSharp.Codemode and an embed-docs entry. Prerequisite for codemode.worker-admission-limit; pairs with codemode.stop-without-exit-wait.

rows.change: The coding agent's codemode tool admits at most two live workers across all sessions, counting cancelled workers until they actually exit through acquireWorker(); a run over the limit fails with "Codemode worker limit reached (2 workers are still running or shutting down). Retry after they exit."
rows.notes: PiSharp's executor caps concurrent model calls (MaxConcurrentModelCalls = 4) but not live workers, so repeated timeouts can pile up child processes. Depends on codemode.worker-lifetime-hooks. A later upstream bullet in another group turns the rejection into waiting for capacity; port the final behaviour and the matching docs once.

rows.change: At the process-wide worker limit, codemode scripts wait in arrival order for a free worker instead of failing at once. The wait honours abort, counts toward timeout_ms and is capped at 60 seconds, after which the script fails without running. PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS (a positive integer, read per call) raises the default limit of two.
rows.notes: PiSharp has no worker admission at all: each execution starts its own worker (CodemodeSandbox.cs:228), so it never had the 1.3.0 "worker limit reached" failure. This row depends on the 1.3.0 admission rows owned by group A (coding-agent@1.3.0/Fixed#4 and codemode@1.3.0/Added#2, the acquireWorker hook). src/PiSharp.Cli/docs/codemode.md is a byte copy of docs/codemode.md and changes with it. Port the error texts from execute.ts.

TaskState, TaskGraphState and TaskInspection gain a sleeping status, and generation retry backoffs, deferred-response polls and compaction retry backoffs sleep instead of waiting inside a running phase (a record stored mid-backoff by an older version sleeps again on resume; a deferred poll whose model is gone fails no_model once due).
rows.notes: PiSharp has ITaskRuntime.SleepAsync(until, context) (TypesTasks.cs:98), which waits inside the phase. PiSharp-only callers must move to sleepUntil phases: recurring jobs (decision 0009; Hosting Apps/Jobs.cs:590 and :798, Apps/JobBranches.cs:266) and custom agent workflows (decision 0012; CustomAgents Workflows/Engine/Composition.cs:313, WorkflowEngine.cs:115). SQLite and SQL Server task tables need the sleeping status (durable.sqlite-schema-v2). Depends on durable.host-timers (the timers that resume sleepers); pairs with durable.wake. Upstream renumbered the examples (13-recovery is 12-recovery, 24-child-tasks is 23-child-tasks).

rows.change: HarnessOptions.setTimer (and createSession()'s) arms every timer of the Session, the scheduler and its tasks (progress throttles, idle document and context eviction, sleeps), so with now they run on a host or fake clock. A foreground timer the host throws on or declines falls back to setTimeout and is reported once, a background one is declined; TaskRuntime.setTimer() paces work inside a phase without waiting for it, and ToolExecutionApi.now() reads the Harness clock.
rows.notes: PiSharp already has a .NET seam for part of this: HarnessOptions.TimeProvider (Harness/Types.cs:747-749) arms sleeps and idle context expiry. Missing: the Session's timers (createSession, document retention, progress throttles), the foreground/background split with its fallback report, ITaskRuntime.SetTimer and IToolExecutionApi.Now. The area decides whether setTimer maps onto TimeProvider (a fake TimeProvider for tests) or a new delegate; a .NET timer never keeps the process alive, so 'background' needs no unref. Code that builds ITaskRuntime or IToolExecutionApi by hand must add the members (none outside tests today). The Progress clock is chord@1.4.0/Added#4 (group F), ported here in PiSharp's Chord subset (Harness/Output.cs). durable.codemode-harness-clock depends on Now().

rows.change: Harness.wake() says when the Session next needs a running process (active while work can run, at for the earliest sleep), and HarnessOptions.onWake is called after open and whenever that changes. With onWake set the Harness keeps no timer for sleeps, so a host can stop or hibernate and call resume() at the time it was given.
rows.notes: No counterpart today. Depends on durable.durable-sleep; 1.5.0 makes wake() cheap (durable.scheduler-idle-index), and a read-only Harness's wake() is always inactive (durable.read-only-harness). PiSharp-only: the device host (decision 0008, Hosting DurableDeviceHost.cs) and recurring job schedules (decision 0009, Hosting JobSchedules.cs) keep sessions open and arm their own timers; onWake would let them close idle sessions and reopen at the wake time. Record whether they adopt it; nothing requires them to.

rows.change: Open counts the restarts of each task a crash, eviction or reset cut off (TaskRecord.restarts; a close writes the tasks it stopped back as pending uncounted, and a newly committed state starts the count over). At settings.restartLimit (default 5) the task ends instead of running again: a tool call gets an error result with diagnostic restart_limit, a compaction fails into pi.live.compactionFailure, a generation ends its run with runFailure reason restart_limit, and an extension task ends faulted with { reason: 'restart_limit' }; built-in tasks are reported as task_interrupted, extension tasks as task_faulted. 1.4.0's parking (Harness.retryTask(), the restart_limit blocked reason, the task_parked report) is removed again in 1.5.0.
rows.notes: PiSharp counts no restarts: a task cut off by every crash reruns forever. Port 1.5.0's end state only; 1.4.0's parking and retryTask() were removed before 1.5.0 and get no C# surface. TaskRecord (Types.cs:745) gains restarts, a record JSON field the compat cases compare with upstream's. Depends on durable.run-failure (the restart_limit reason), durable.reports (task_interrupted, task_faulted) and durable.telemetry (report attributes). The crash suite (decision 0005 'Crash tests') needs cases at the limit. PiSharp-only extension tasks (recurring jobs in Hosting Apps/Jobs.cs; workflow and team tasks in CustomAgents) end faulted after five cut-offs in a row instead of rerunning.

rows.change: A generation whose model request was in flight when the host died no longer resends it on open: the attempt counts as failed under settings.retry, its partial becomes an aborted entry, the next attempt waits for the backoff shown in pi.live.generation.retry, and with no retry left the run ends with runFailure reason interrupted (its inputs settle unanswered). A deferred poll whose fetch was in flight is charged the same way and polls the same deferred response again; a close still resends, and a charge that is itself cut off restartLimit times ends the run restart_limit.
rows.notes: PiSharp resends the request after a crash, and its crash cases at the request and streaming checkpoints rely on that (decision 0005 'Crash tests': exactly one answer per turn); they change to expect a charged attempt, the backoff and a runFailure once retries run out. Depends on durable.durable-sleep (the backoff sleeps), durable.restart-limit and durable.run-failure. NativeDurableModels implements no deferred responses (decision 0005 'Model adapter'), so the deferred-poll half is covered with faux models only.

rows.change: The scheduler's per-commit work no longer grows with the number of conversations: after a commit it re-checks idleness only for the conversations above the tasks that became live or ended, expires idle context ranges from an expiry-ordered index, and wake() takes the earliest sleep from the sleeping tasks and scans live tasks only while nothing runs. Before, every commit re-walked every conversation read in the last contextRetentionMs.
rows.notes: Scheduler.cs ports v1.2.0's scheduler as a whole (decision 0005 'Scheduler'), per-commit walk included. Depends on durable.wake for wake() and on durable.group-commit (the scheduler's commit path changes there). Helps the device host, which serves many sessions (decision 0008); record the benchmark in docs/durable-benchmarks.md.

rows.change: defineDoc() and defineDocFamily() require a checkpointWhen predicate on every definition; there is no default. Every built-in document states its policy: task-scoped documents that retire with their task use () => false, and code mode's rewindable store writes a base every 64 deltas.
rows.notes: Every Documents.DefineXDoc takes checkpointWhen = null (Documents.cs:110-158). Making it required breaks every PiSharp-only definition listed (custom agents, decision 0012; device host, apps and jobs, decisions 0008-0010; ask_user_question and plan mode, decision 0005), and each must choose a policy (() => false keeps today's deltas-only behaviour). Upstream's code mode checkpoint test is new (codemode-checkpoints.test.ts).

rows.change: Document, conversation view and task graph watches are Chord's WatchHandle, built on Chord's one Watch implementation, and Durable re-exports WatchHandle, WatchEnd, WatchCall and NativeWatchCall. A listener takes one tagged call before the context, { kind: 'value', value, ops, retired } (Chord's { kind: 'failed' } call never comes from Durable); WatchEnd is tagged by kind: stopped, aborted (was cancelled), ended (was session_closed), listener_error and failed (was session_failed), retired is no longer an end, and an ended watch drops its listener and every reference into its Session.
rows.notes: PiSharp's IWatchHandle<T>, WatchEnd(Reason, Error) and WatchEndReason (TypesSession.cs:161-218) and Session/Observation.cs port v1.2.0's observation.ts, which upstream deleted. The Chord side (chord@1.5.0/Added#8, Added#9, Breaking Changes#3, #5, #6 and #7) is group F, phase 6: phase 4 ports the subset Durable needs into PiSharp.Durable/Chord, as decision 0005 §1 does for the rest of Chord, and phase 6 reconciles. PiSharp-only listeners change shape: Hosting Apps/Jobs.cs:780 and Feeds.cs, CustomAgents Teams/Messaging.cs:293, Orchestration.cs:130, :393 and :548, Workflows/Engine/Composition.cs:300, Durable.Tools Interaction/UserInteraction.cs:131, and pisharp durable (DurableRuntime.cs). Land with durable.document-watch-address, durable.watch-folding and durable.observers.

rows.change: A document watch follows its address (kind, scope and key) instead of one incarnation: DocumentWatch<T> is WatchHandle<Readonly<T>> without null, a retirement arrives as the next call with retired: true, the last value and no ops, and a document created at the address later arrives on the same watch as [['r', value]]. A task document's watch ends ended once the retirement call of the commit that makes its task terminal has returned, and a watch pins the incarnation at its address, nothing while it is absent.
rows.notes: PiSharp ends a watch at retirement with a last [['r', null]] frame and reason retired (Observation.cs, RETIREMENT_OPERATIONS). PiSharp-only code waiting on task-scoped documents relies on that end: ask_user_question and plan approval (Durable.Tools Interaction/UserInteraction.cs:131; pisharp.interaction retires with the call), job approvals (Hosting Apps/Jobs.cs:780, pisharp.job-approval), workflow runs (CustomAgents Workflows/Engine/Composition.cs:300) and team mailboxes (CustomAgents Teams/Messaging.cs:293). Each must test retired and stop a watch whose document may stay retired, or the watch lives until the Session ends. Depends on durable.watch-handles.

rows.change: Document, conversation view and task graph watches deliver the commits made while their listener runs (or before start()) in one callback: the newest value, the commits' operations folded (appends to one string join, sets of one field keep the last) and the newest commit's Context. Past 10,000 pending operations the callback gets one root replacement; before, each commit was its own callback and more than 100 pending commits became a root replacement.
rows.notes: PiSharp buffers one frame per commit with the 100-frame limit (Observation.cs header). Folding is Chord's PendingOps (chord@1.5.0/Added#12, group F), ported into PiSharp.Durable/Chord/Delta for phase 4. PiSharp-only consumers that expect one call per commit: the device server's agent and document frames (Server AgentFrames.cs, decision 0008: 'one batch of pi-durable events per commit'), the web agent's per-tab mux (decision 0011) and pisharp durable's TUI (DurableRuntime.cs). Depends on durable.watch-handles.

rows.change: The Chord state getters Session.documentState(), Conversation.viewState() and Harness.taskGraph() and the DocumentState type are removed; callers use watchDoc(), Conversation.watch() and Harness.watchTaskGraph(), and Durable no longer uses Chord's replicatedState().
rows.notes: PiSharp still exposes DocumentStateAsync, ViewStateAsync and the task graph state over its ReplicatedState port (Chord/ReplicatedState.cs). PiSharp-only callers: Server DeviceService.cs:390 (a one-off view read), Durable.Tools Interaction/UserInteraction.cs:74, and pisharp durable (DurableRuntime.cs:321 and :644, which follows the view state across revisions). Whether ReplicatedState.cs stays for Chord (phase 6) or goes with Durable's last use is group F's call. Depends on durable.watch-handles.

rows.change: Session.observeDoc(), Harness.observeConversation() and Harness.observeTaskGraph() attach a synchronous Observer<T> atomically on the Session line and return an Observation<T> (value, detach()); advance(call, context) gets every change unfolded as memory adopts it (a stored commit once its storage call settled, a deferred one before it is stored), so it may only record it: no awaits, Session calls or throws. end(end) takes the watch's WatchEnd shapes and comes once, a throwing observer (or one whose advance rejects) is reported as listener_error and detached, and a Session close ends observers failed with 'session closed' (ended stays for a task document retired with its task). Document, view and task graph watches are built on them (spec §9.1).
rows.notes: No synchronous observer API today; PiSharp's watches sit on Observation.cs's source attachments. In .NET 'no awaits' means a callback that returns, and a Task-returning advance that faults counts as rejected. Chord's self.follow, which the close-as-failed rule serves, is group F (phase 6). Depends on durable.watch-handles; durable.observe-commits and durable.conversation-window use the same shapes.

rows.change: subscribeCommits(listener) becomes observeCommits(observer) with the observer shape { advance(publication, context), end(end) }, returning { detach() }; its observation has no value. end comes once (ended after the last publication at close, failed when the Session fails), and an observer that throws or whose advance rejects is reported, detached and ended listener_error, where a throwing listener used to stay subscribed.
rows.notes: PiSharp has SubscribeCommits with synchronous and asynchronous overloads (TypesSession.cs; decision 0005 'Storage failures', second mapping). PiSharp-only callers: the device host's change notifications (HostedSession.cs:747) and pisharp durable (DurableRuntime.cs:333). After durable.deferred-commits they see partials only once stored. Depends on durable.observers; ordering is durable.commit-publication.

rows.change: DocumentCommitChange is tagged: a change is { type: 'document', kind: 'change', record, conversationId, version, value, ops } and a retirement { type: 'document', kind: 'retire', record, conversationId }, where a retirement used to be value: null with version undefined.
rows.notes: TypesSession.cs:137 has DocumentCommitChange(Record, ConversationId, int? Version, JsonObjectValue? Value, ...) with a null value for a retirement; in C# a kind discriminator or two derived records. PiSharp-only commit consumers (the device host's HostedSession.cs, pisharp durable's DurableRuntime.cs) must not test for a null value. Land with durable.observe-commits.

rows.change: SessionEnd (Session.closed, Harness.closed) is tagged by kind: { kind: 'closed' } or { kind: 'failed', error } instead of reason.
rows.notes: SessionEnd(SessionEndReason Reason, Exception? Error) at TypesSession.cs:199-208 becomes a Kind; a rename in C#. PiSharp-only readers: the device host (HostedSession.cs:868) and pisharp durable (DurableRuntime.cs:442 and :736).

rows.change: Session.commit(), Conversation.commit(), TaskRuntime.commit() and a tool's api.commit() take { persistence: { kind: 'deferred', withinMs? } }: a commit that changes only existing latest-history, initial-fork conversation documents is adopted in memory and shown to watches at once, and stored with the next commit that reads or writes the document, before the document leaves memory, at close, or within withinMs (default settings.progress.persistWithinMs, 1,000 ms); any other write makes it immediate. The Harness defers its throttled partial-answer and running-tool-output commits, a tool slot's running status, a nested call's final arguments and a generation's attempt, so a crash loses up to about a second of streamed content, and subscribeCommits() sees them only once stored.
rows.notes: PiSharp stores every throttled partial (one storage transaction each, as v1.2.0). A stream that crashes before its first store now leaves no aborted entry and its usage is not recorded; the crash cases at the streaming-partial checkpoint (decision 0005 'Crash tests') follow. PiSharp-only: the device host notifies clients from SubscribeCommits (HostedSession.cs:747) and stops seeing partials; its agent stream must come from watches (durable.watch-events-removed). settings.progress.persistWithinMs: 0 restores per-partial stores. Depends on durable.partial-commit-appends (partial-changes.ts) and durable.commit-publication.

rows.change: A Session no longer holds its line while a commit is stored: commits that arrive while a storage call is in flight go out together in the next call, each with its own seq and outcome, and a job runs while earlier commits are being stored until it touches a key one of them wrote (a record, a document, a conversation's entries, a task's membership or cancellation state), then waits until that commit is stored and published. Outcomes are delivered in line order, every job after a commit that fails the Session gets SessionFailed, at most 256 jobs wait for their outcome, a wait whose commit is still being stored at close ends with the closed error (the commit is still stored and published), and cancellation is checked when a job starts.
rows.notes: The deepest runtime change. PiSharp's Session line (Session.cs, with decision 0005's .NET mappings: line jobs, Session.Defer, the storage lease) awaits each CommitAsync before the next job. Port writer.ts and keys.ts as the line's write path over durable.storage-commit-batches. Upstream measured about 5 to 440 runs per second at 128 conversations over 4 ms storage; record PiSharp's own numbers in docs/durable-benchmarks.md. PiSharp-only SQL Server storage (decision 0007), with its network round trips, gains most. Depends on durable.storage-commit-batches; durable.commit-publication and durable.read-caches come with it.

rows.change: A stored commit is published after its storage call settled, in line order, the commits of one call a macrotask apart and inside the storage's publishing() scope: the read caches and memory adopt it, then its telemetry events and Durable's own observers (watches, views, the task graph, the scheduler, waits) run, and observeCommits() observers run one microtask later, before the waits it resolves and the abort signals it fires. A throwing Durable observer fails the Session after commit() returned while the commit stands, a commit Storage rejects after adopting it (a failed JSONL reclaim) is still published and its waits resolve before the Session fails, commit listeners are read when the dispatch runs, and a newly marked running task's abort signal fires after them.
rows.notes: PiSharp publishes on the Session line after each commit (decision 0005: work deferred during publication runs right after it, as upstream's microtasks). .NET has no macrotask/microtask split, so the area defines the C# order (Durable observers, then commit observers, then waits and abort signals) and pins it with the ported adoption and observer tests. The Fixed#8 case matters for PiSharp's JSONL storage, whose reclaim can fail after adoption. Depends on durable.group-commit and durable.observe-commits.

rows.change: A normal agent run makes no storage reads: the Session keeps recently read conversation, task and submission records (bounded by count, and by live work for tasks), the newest entry of each conversation and the task documents of live tasks, and the scheduler keeps the context range of a running conversation. Read results (tx.task(), tx.conversation(), getTask(), runtime.entry(), published entries) are frozen objects shared with these caches, and mutating one throws.
rows.notes: PiSharp's records and JSON values are immutable already (Context.cs header: upstream's freezeJson has no counterpart), so the frozen-result half holds by construction; the caches are missing. Depends on durable.group-commit (the caches sit under the writer). SQL Server storage gains the most.

rows.change: ConversationView.entries is a window over the fork-aware transcript Conversation.entries() scans, in entry ID order, with head markers appended in place instead of cutting the entries before them: a watch starts with the newest 50 entries, appends new ones, and past 100 drops the oldest in one splice down to 50, setting ConversationView.before. Conversation.watch(context, window?) and Harness.observeConversation(id, observer, context, window?) take a ConversationWindow (from, min default 50, max default 2 x min; bounds that are not integers, or max below min, reject with RangeError), each watch and observer has its own window, and first values and overflow replacements hold at most max entries.
rows.notes: PiSharp's view carries the active transcript (cut at the head marker). PiSharp-only readers that treat it as the model's context: pisharp durable's TUI (DurableTuiView.cs:197-200 sync and rebuild the transcript from it, :441 counts context tokens), the device service's entries read (DeviceService.cs:391) and the client transcript builder (decision 0008). They move to Conversation.context() for what the model sees and to ConversationTranscript for rendering. Depends on durable.observers; land with durable.conversation-transcript and before durable.watch-events-removed.

rows.change: ConversationTranscript keeps what a client has of one conversation over any ConversationView: merge(view) returns the view with items (entries, a gap where a later window did not continue it, and an earlier marker until the start is loaded), loadEarlier() and fillGap() page entries through a loader such as Conversation.entries(), and resume is the window that continues it after a drop. A merge costs O(items) and returns the same items array when it adds nothing; concurrent loads of one page are shared.
rows.notes: New upstream file with no PiSharp counterpart. Name collision: PiSharp.Durable.Client's Transcript.cs (PiSharp-only, decision 0008) already builds renderable transcript items from entries and pi.live for the device's /transcript route, the hub and terminals. The owner decides whether it is rebuilt on ConversationTranscript (gaps, paging, resume) or stays the client layer above it. Depends on durable.conversation-window.

rows.change: pi.live.runFailure (RunFailure, RunFailureReason) records why the newest run ended without an answer (model_error, no_model, aborted, reset, faulted or orphaned) with the run's task and inputs and a detail where one exists; the commit that ends the run sets it and a later commit that starts a run removes it. pi.live is therefore no longer empty after such a run, and idleness is run === undefined.
rows.notes: PiSharp learns of an unanswered run only from run_end events. RunFailureReason also gains interrupted and restart_limit (durable.interrupted-request, durable.restart-limit), nothing_to_answer (durable.continue-submissions) and turn_limit (durable.turn-limit); declare the C# enum once with every 1.5.0 value. PiSharp-only code that shows failures from events or tests idleness as an empty pi.live (pisharp durable's notices, the client model and the web agent's chat views, decisions 0008 and 0011) should read runFailure and run.

rows.change: watchEvents() and its types AgentEvent, AgentEventStream, SnapshotEvent, MessageChange and ToolEventCall are removed with spec §9.4 (src/harness/events.ts and test/harness-events.test.ts are deleted): a renderer renders the conversation view, whose operations carry the same deltas the events did. The changelog maps every event to its state: pi.live.run, generation.message and retry, the tools and nestedTools slots, compactions, runFailure, pi.inbox, pi.agent, pi.usage and Submission.status().
rows.notes: The largest collision with PiSharp-only surfaces. The device protocol (decisions 0008 and 0010) is built on watchEvents: Hosting's AgentEventFeed (Feeds.cs:28) feeds the server's agent stream, which sends a snapshot and one batch of pi-durable events per commit verbatim (AgentFrames.cs); the client reduces them (Client Models.cs; Wire.cs passes AgentEvent.ToJson() through), the hub multiplexes them (Web Hub/StreamMux.cs), and so do the web agent (AgentViewHub.cs, decision 0011) and pisharp durable attach. The owner decides: move the device protocol to view state (conversation watch frames plus ConversationTranscript), or keep a PiSharp-only event projection derived from view operations so the wire protocol stays. The compat cases compare agent events with the v1.2.0 events.json captures (decision 0005), which v1.5.0 has no counterpart for. Depends on durable.conversation-window, durable.conversation-transcript and durable.run-failure.

rows.change: CompactionStatus.reason and CompactionFailure.reason in pi.live are renamed trigger (what started the compaction), leaving reason for why a run failed. pi.live becomes version 2: its migrate renames the field in a stored version 1 value when it is read, and the next commit stores version 2, which version 1 code cannot read.
rows.notes: pi.live is version 1 in PiSharp (Live.cs:25); the migrate chain to version 2 (this row) and version 3 (turns, durable.turn-limit) should land as one. PiSharp 1.2.0.x cannot read a conversation PiSharp 1.5.0 wrote to; record it in decision 0005 and the release notes. PiSharp-only readers of compactionFailure.reason: pisharp durable's 'Compaction failed (<reason>)' line (decision 0005 area l), the client model, the hub and the web agent's chat views.

rows.change: TaskGraphNode.blocked says why a live task cannot run (missing_task, task_too_old or migration_failed; 1.4.0's restart_limit is gone again in 1.5.0), and the task graph follows registry changes and failed migrations outside any commit. TaskInspection.state uses TaskState's word: { kind: 'pending', migrates } replaces ready.
rows.notes: PiSharp has BlockedReason and TaskInspectionKind.Ready for inspect() (Harness/Types.cs) but no blocked field on TaskGraphNode (TaskGraph.cs:95). PiSharp-only graph readers, the device server's task graph stream (Server DeviceStreams.cs:54 through Hosting Feeds.cs's TaskGraphFeed) and the web UI, gain a blocked reason to show. The sleeping state is durable.durable-sleep.

rows.change: HarnessOptions.onReport(report) takes one Report tagged by kind with the error inside: storage_failed (was session_failed), task_faulted, migration_failed, task_outdated (reason task_too_old or migration_failed), task_error with the task and the extension that installed it, extension_error, host_error with the failing HostCallback, listener_error, and in 1.5.0 task_interrupted. A faulted phase is reported (task_faulted), not only recorded in its outcome, and runtime.report(error, from) takes a ReportFrom tagged { kind: 'extension', extension? } or { kind: 'host', callback }.
rows.notes: PiSharp's OnReport is Action<Exception> (Harness/Types.cs:754) and ITaskRuntime.Report(Exception) (TypesTasks.cs:95), the v1.2.0 shape. Port 1.5.0's one-argument Report directly; 1.4.0's (error, info) form never reached PiSharp. PiSharp-only consumers pass the exception through and must move to Report or unwrap it: the device host's OnReport(sessionId, Exception) (HostedSession.cs:729, DurableDeviceOptions.cs:66), pisharp durable (DurableRuntime.cs:154), pisharp durable serve (DurableServe.cs:164), custom agent teams (AgentTeam.cs:94) and the web agent (DeviceHostService.cs:77). The pi.durable.report telemetry event is durable.telemetry; task_interrupted is durable.restart-limit.

rows.change: HarnessOptions.telemetry emits the content-free DURABLE_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA: pi.durable.submit admission spans, task phase spans (extension tasks included), committed entry and submission events, running phase-change checkpoints and nested-tool replay events, optional phase-duration and live-task metrics, and a pi.durable.report event and pi.durable.reports counter for every onReport report. Optional propagation stores opaque trace carriers on submissions and tasks (TaskOptions.trace takes a carrier or 'root'), creation-time links join inputs that share a run, failed phases get fixed error categories, and generation and compaction pass their phase context to pi-ai requests.
rows.notes: No telemetry in PiSharp's durable port. Depends on the telemetry.* rows (phase 3: the pi-telemetry port with spans, links, metrics and propagation) and on pi-ai request tracing (ai@1.4.0/Added#4); Context.telemetry is chord@1.4.0/Added#2 and Breaking Changes#1 (group F), ported here in DurableContext. PiSharp.Durable may reference only Contracts and AI (decision 0005 §4), so the owner decides where the telemetry abstractions live for Durable to use them. Trace carriers are new fields of submission and task records, which the compat cases compare with upstream's. The device host (decision 0008) could export these spans later; nothing requires it.

rows.change: A telemetry adapter that throws while a commit is published (its pi.durable.entry or pi.durable.submission event, pi.durable.tasks.active) no longer rejects the commit or leaves the views and the scheduler without it: it is reported as host_error with the new HostCallback 'telemetry', and the commit resolves. A throwing report metric or report event is dropped.
rows.notes: Depends on durable.telemetry and durable.reports: HostCallback arrives with 1.4.0's report info, which PiSharp lacks (OnReport is Action<Exception>). Exhaustive switches over the C# HostCallback enum need the case; PiSharp-only report handlers have none yet.

rows.change: settings.compaction.modelOverrides, keyed by exact 'provider/modelId', replaces the harness-wide compaction fields for that model field by field (compactionPolicy()), so one harness serves small- and large-window models; the threshold check, overflow recovery and the compaction task each use the entry of the model they act for.
rows.notes: PiSharp's HarnessSettings.Compaction is a plain CompactionPolicy. PiSharp-only per-session compaction in the device host (Hosting SessionCompaction.cs, decision 0008) sets the harness-wide policy; check that it composes with overrides instead of replacing them. Settings can be a provider after durable.host-option-providers.

rows.change: settings.afterFailedRun decides the inputs queued behind a run that fails with model_error or no_model: keep them queued (keep, the default), start the next run with them (continue), or settle them unanswered with reason run_failed (withdraw).
rows.notes: PiSharp has no such setting. In 1.5.0 the policy also governs turn_limit (durable.turn-limit), and a continue submission places a failed run's queue first (durable.continue-submissions). The device host and web UI (decisions 0008 and 0011) read queued inputs from pi.inbox and could expose the setting per session.

rows.change: HarnessOptions.identity (a pi-ai ClientIdentity) sets the User-Agent and provider attribution of every model request through the Harness, hooks and tools included; api.models in tools and hooks is a wrapper of the host's Models that adds the identity, not the same object.
rows.notes: Depends on ai@1.4.0/Added#1 and agent@1.4.0/Added#1 (group B: ClientIdentity in PiSharp.AI). 0013 design point 'Identity': PiSharp identifies as the Pi version it tracks (user agent pi/<version> (<platform>; <runtime>; <arch>)). NativeDurableModels and the CLI's DurableModels stream over PiSharp.AI transports, so the identity must reach them; the device host and the web agent (decisions 0008 and 0011) open Harnesses and should pass the same identity.

rows.change: HarnessOptions.models and HarnessOptions.settings also accept a function returning the current value, like env: generation, compaction, hooks and tools call it at each use (api.models reads the current value at each access), so a host replaces its model configuration or settings without reopening the Harness. A plain object still works.
rows.notes: HarnessOptions.Models is a required IDurableModels and Settings a HarnessSettings (Harness/Types.cs:733-736); a C# shape is Func<IDurableModels> and Func<HarnessSettings?> alternatives. A throwing provider is reported as host_error with callback models or settings (durable.reports). The device host (decision 0008, HostedSession.cs) changes a session's model and settings by committing or reopening; record whether it moves to providers.

rows.change: HarnessOptions.readOnly opens a Harness as a viewer of a session another process drives: open leaves running tasks as committed instead of recovering them, every commit with writes rejects with ReadOnlySession before it reaches Storage, resume() and every call that would run tasks reject with it, and wake() is always inactive.

Name collision: the device host's 'read-only switch' (HostedSession.cs:356, DurableDeviceOptions.cs:58) removes tools from an agent and is unrelated; keep the two apart in names and docs. rows.change: submit({ type: 'continue' }) starts a run on the context as it is, without a user message: only an idle conversation admits one (a busy one throws ConversationBusy, it never queues), items a failed run left queued are placed first and join the run, and a context that ends in an answer has nothing to continue. SubmissionRecord gains a type 'continue' variant (placed without entry, done with answer, unanswered), ConversationHandle.submit() takes any SubmissionDraft, and a generation whose context does not end in a user message or tool results ends its run unanswered with the new RunFailureReason nothing_to_answer without a request, so an empty conversation no longer faults its generation.
rows.notes: SubmissionRecord (Types.cs) is input-only today; code that narrows a record by status alone must also check its type. Depends on durable.run-failure (runFailure, run.first) and durable.telemetry (the pi.durable.submit root span). PiSharp-only hosts that build submissions (the device API and Hosting SubmissionAnswers.cs, decision 0010; the web agent, decision 0011) could offer a Continue action after a failed run; record whether they do.

rows.change: AgentState.maxTurns (configure({ maxTurns }); null clears; RangeError for anything but an integer of 1 or more) bounds the tool rounds one run takes: the round that reaches it runs its tools, then the run ends unanswered with RunFailureReason turn_limit and settings.afterFailedRun decides the queued inputs. pi.live.run has a required turns count (0 at every run start and after an onYield continuation), task-owned children and forks inherit the limit, and pi.live becomes version 3, whose migrate adds turns: 0 to a stored run without it.
rows.notes: No turn limit in PiSharp. Depends on durable.run-failure, durable.after-failed-run and durable.live-compaction-trigger (pi.live version 2; the migrate chain to version 3 lands once). PiSharp-only: custom agent subagents and workflows (decision 0012) bound their own loops and could set maxTurns; the device host's agent settings could expose it.

rows.change: whenIdle: 'reject' on an input submission makes an idle conversation reject it with the new ConversationIdle and write nothing, so it never starts a run; with whenBusy: 'steer' it steers the current run or is refused in one admission, instead of a host's check and a separate submit that can race the run's end. A known request ID still returns its submission.
rows.notes: PiSharp-only: the device API passes whenBusy through to SubmissionDraft (Server DurableDeviceApi.cs:203-212, Hosting HostedSession.cs:269); exposing whenIdle there is a protocol choice under decision 0010.

rows.change: Conversation.submit(tx, draft) admits a submission inside the caller's commit (Harness.commit(), Conversation.commit()) with the same rules as submit(draft, context) and returns its ID, and ConversationHandle.submit(tx, draft) does the same inside a task's or tool's own commit, so a host checks its own documents and pi.live, admits and writes its state in one commit that stores all of it or none. It must come before the commit's first table write, once per commit, and throws ReadAfterWrite otherwise; the pi.durable.submit span covers the admission only.
rows.notes: No counterpart. PiSharp-only hosts that write their own documents and then submit in a second commit could merge the two: recurring jobs' start receipts (Hosting Apps/Jobs.cs, pisharp.job-start), app tools' entry receipts (Apps/AppTools.cs) and workflow starts (CustomAgents Workflows/Hosting/WorkflowTools.cs); record whether they adopt it. durable.after-run-tasks uses it (a run-end task admits its follow-up in its own commit).

rows.change: HookApi.entry() and entries(), and TaskRuntime.entries(), read the conversation's raw history, which compaction never changes, so a range bounded by entry IDs reads the same before and after a compaction and on a rerun.
rows.notes: PiSharp's ITaskRuntime has EntryAsync and ContextAsync (TypesTasks.cs:85-91) and IConversation has EntriesAsync (Harness/Types.cs:1020), but IHookApi has no entry reads and ITaskRuntime no ranged one. durable.after-run-tasks depends on it (run.first, answer, last).

rows.change: GenerationHooks.afterRun(run, api) returns { tasks }, built with the typed runEndTask(task, input), after a run answered (a final answer or a terminate round; not an onYield continuation, a failure or an abort). The answer is committed and the inputs settle done first; the generation then creates the tasks as its children and waits for them, keeping pi.live.run (with run.afterRun) and the conversation busy, so idle waits include them, Stop aborts them and a crash resumes them, and input queued meanwhile starts the next run once they are terminal. run names the run's entries first (pi.live.run.first, carried into runFailure.first), answer and last; a broken request is reported and skipped.
rows.notes: No counterpart. Depends on durable.entry-reads, durable.submit-in-commit and durable.run-failure. Upstream's example 32 (tests after edits) is a ready demo. PiSharp-only: custom agent workflows (decision 0012) and recurring job runs (decision 0009) implement their own after-run steps as tasks; record whether they move to afterRun.

rows.change: A tool round with control.handoff no longer ends the run on the tool-calling answer: the handoff's pi.reset entry is written and the same run continues with a new generation in the new context, so the submission settles with the eventual answer. Queued writes and selected steers are placed after the handoff text, follow-ups wait for the run's final boundary, and a queued reset still ends the run unanswered with reason reset.
rows.notes: Generation.cs:735 ends the run on terminate or handoff (v1.2.0). Plan mode's exit tool (Durable.Tools PlanMode/ExitPlanModeTool.cs) uses terminate, which is unchanged; no PiSharp-only handoff user was found.

rows.change: A call to a tool its request did not offer gets a pi.tool task like any call, flagged unoffered: true in its input and its pi.live.tools slot, instead of a result the generation wrote itself: the task resolves nothing (a deferred tool the agent still has never runs), settles tool_unavailable and runs afterTool, whose control now counts toward the round. Its slot starts pending with a taskId, its result entry lands in a later commit than the answer, controls apply in call order, and pi.tool becomes version 3 and pi.generation version 2, which an older Harness leaves blocked (task_too_old).
rows.notes: PiSharp has pi.tool version 2 and pi.generation version 1 (Tool.cs:54, Generation.cs:39), and Generation.cs:720 still answers unoffered calls without a task. Both version bumps are record compatibility changes: PiSharp 1.2.0.x leaves such tasks blocked. Depends on durable.after-tool-every-result.

rows.change: afterTool runs on every result a tool task writes, including the Harness's own error results (tool_unavailable, invalid_arguments with the arguments as the model sent them, blocked, interrupted, restart_limit, aborted, abandoned), which the diagnostic code tells apart. Such a result is bounded by the tool's output limits after the hooks, never keeps a structuredOutput and applies control only when the call completes; past restartLimit cut-offs the hooks no longer run, and an abort's hooks delay Conversation.abort().
rows.notes: PiSharp runs afterTool only for executed calls (v1.2.0). No PiSharp-only afterTool hooks exist outside the core, so the collision is limited to tests and to user extensions, which must check result diagnostics before casting arguments. Depends on durable.restart-limit (restart_limit results); pairs with durable.unoffered-tool-calls.

rows.change: GenerationHooks.beforeProviderRequest({ model, payload }, api) replaces the provider request body of a generation request, for that request only: the body is in the provider API's format, hooks chain in extension order each time pi-ai builds a body, a throw is reported and the chain continues, and compaction requests do not use it.
rows.notes: Upstream passes the chain as pi-ai's onPayload stream option. IDurableModels streams over PiSharp.AI's native transports (decision 0005 'Model adapter'), which must hand the provider body to a callback on every route, the CLI's live routes included; check what PiSharp.AI's payload hook already offers before adding a durable stream option. No PiSharp-only surface is affected.

rows.change: A generation records the Pi thinking level its request asked for as thinkingLevel on the stored assistant message, also after polling a deferred response, as pi-agent-core's agent loop does.

rows.change: Partial commits of a streamed answer no longer reassign every growing text, thinking and tool-call argument string in full: partial-changes.ts plans what each commit changes, appends new text with Chord's appendText() (an append op recorded without comparing the old and new strings), and applies argument changes from the Harness's own incremental parse of the streamed argument text. Before, a 500 KB tool call cost about 20 s of CPU and a 100 MB heap peak.
rows.notes: PiSharp's AssignJson (Json.cs:17) assigns the partial message leaf by leaf, and the tracker compares each string with its previous value (Tracker.cs:499), so a growing string is read in full on every commit, as upstream before the fix. appendText is chord@1.5.0/Added#14 (group F), ported here in PiSharp's Chord subset; the incremental argument parse is StreamingJsonParser (ai@1.5.0/Added#2, group C). durable.deferred-commits reworks the same files; land this first.

rows.change: Append ops, nested call error summaries, task span error messages and code mode call previews are cut with ownedSlice(), which copies the characters, because V8 represents a slice of 13 or more characters as a view that keeps the whole source string alive; a conversation watcher had held well over 100 MB for a 140 KB answer and a 140 KB tool call.
rows.notes: The Chord half is chord@1.5.0/Added#13 and Fixed#3 (group F). Task span error messages arrive with durable.telemetry; cut them with a range there too.
rows.evidence: V8-specific retention: a .NET string is never a view of another, and a range copies just its characters. Append ops: src/PiSharp.Durable/Chord/Delta/Diff.cs:81 and :91, src/PiSharp.Durable/Chord/Delta/Tracker.cs:507 and :514 cut with ranges; Tracker.cs:377 emits AppendText's own text and Draft.cs:251 builds the new value by concatenation, holding no larger string. Nested call summary: src/PiSharp.Durable/Harness/Tool.cs:707 (error[..MaxSummaryErrorChars]). Code mode previews: src/PiSharp.Durable.Tools/Codemode/Codemode.cs:985 and :996 through JsString.Cut (src/PiSharp.Durable.Tools/Codemode/Describe.cs:174). Test: tests/PiSharp.Durable.Tests/Chord/DeltaAppendTextCases.cs: chord.delta-append-text.keeps-an-op-text-that-does-not-hold-a-larger-string-it-was-cut-from-alive.

rows.change: assignJson treats a __proto__ member the target lacks as absent instead of reading it through to Object.prototype, so a streamed tool call whose arguments gain a __proto__ member after an earlier commit no longer merges into Object.prototype.
rows.notes: Port upstream's harness-json.test.ts case as an authored check that a __proto__ member round-trips as a plain member.

rows.notes: Only the citation moves to v1.5.0, with the new tools-images.test.ts case ported as an authored check that a large image encodes.
rows.evidence: src/PiSharp.Durable.Tools/Tools/ImageProcessor.cs:55: ToBase64 is Convert.ToBase64String(bytes), which sizes the output once and builds no concatenation chain; its output is the same standard base64.

Code mode's other changes in the range: owned slices (durable.owned-slices, no-op), checkpointWhen (durable.checkpoint-when-required), searchTools ranking (durable.tool-search-ranking) and pi-schema (durable.pi-schema-tools).

DurableCodemode calls PiSharp.Codemode's static CodemodeIdentifier.ToIdentifier (src/PiSharp.Durable.Tools/Codemode/Codemode.cs:295), and the Jint engine starts only when a CodemodeSandbox run starts, so the helper loads no engine.

rows.change: tool_search and Code Mode's searchTools() rank like the coding agent: a query that is exactly a tool's name ranks it first, a tool matching more of the query's words ranks above one matching fewer, a query word in the name outweighs any number of mentions in the description, and a tool whose whole name is in the query gets a large bonus. searchTools() indexes the tool's sample and searches namespace instructions as a low-weight field that never lowers a tool's score.

The coding agent's same fix is coding-agent@1.5.0/Fixed#28 (group D1, tools area, phase 2); tool-search.ranking-differential.* compares the two rankers, so both follow the same rules and the differential moves with them. If the merged table maps D1's bullet sameAs this one, this row must also cover main's ranker.

rows.change: The search tokenizer normalizes to NFC, keeps letters, marks and digits of any script, and splits text without spaces between words (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) with Intl.Segmenter's word granularity, ASCII-only text keeping the fast split; only ASCII words are stemmed, so canonically equivalent text such as café and cafe + U+0301 matches.
rows.notes: Search.cs keeps only ASCII letters and digits after its U+0130 expansion (decision 0005 'tool_search'). .NET has no Intl.Segmenter counterpart: dictionary-based word breaking for CJK and Thai needs ICU's word break iterator, which .NET does not expose, or a library, a new dependency the owner must approve; results should match V8's ICU segmentation for the ranking differential. Shared with coding-agent@1.5.0/Fixed#29 (group D1), whose ranker needs the same segmenter; settle it once.

rows.change: The change type of FileSystem.watch() in @earendil-works/pi-durable/env is FileChange (was WatchChange, a name now kept for watch listeners), tagged by kind: { kind: 'paths', paths }, { kind: 'overflow' } or { kind: 'failed', error }, and FileWatcher.close(context) is stop(context).
rows.notes: PiSharp has WatchChange and IFileWatcher in Env/FileSystem.cs. PiSharp-only implementer: plan mode's PlanScope (PlanScope.cs:269 wraps WatchAsync). pi-env's RemoteWatcher follows the same shape (env@1.5.0/Breaking Changes#1, group F, phase 5), so phase 5 builds on this row.

rows.change: isLegacyWslBashPath compares a shell path with %SystemRoot%\System32\bash.exe and %SystemRoot%\Sysnative\bash.exe when SystemRoot is set to an absolute path, and falls back to the C:\Windows pattern only when it is unset; killProcessTree's taskkill path treats an empty SystemRoot as unset.
rows.notes: PiSharp's durable environment uses PiSharp.Tools' ShellDiscovery (LocalExecutionEnv.cs header), whose IsLegacyWslBashPath (ShellDiscovery.cs:38-41) hard-codes C:\Windows. The coding agent's same fix is coding-agent@1.4.0/Fixed#16 (group B); its phase 2 row lands it in ShellDiscovery for both, and phase 4 then re-pins LocalExecutionEnv's citation and ports the env-node case. PiSharp kills through a job object, not taskkill, so that half has no counterpart.

rows.change: Context derivation finds the harness baseline (the first pi.system entry after the head marker, or of the transcript when no earlier entry carries a system message) and moves its system message to the front even past assistant messages; before, only a system message preceded by user messages alone moved. Only the first system message moves, other system messages after an assistant message stay in place, and an extended range carries the baseline forward.
rows.notes: Context.cs:149 LeadWithSystem keeps v1.2.0's rule, so after a compaction that keeps an assistant message, Anthropic and OpenAI Codex requests lead with the kept history and no initial prompt or tool set. context.ts changes again for group commit (durable.group-commit) and the windowed view (durable.conversation-window); this fix is self-contained, so land it first.

rows.change: ToolControl.terminate is typed boolean instead of true, matching pi-agent-core and pi-coding-agent: false is a no-op, and a round ends the run without another request only when every result sets it to true.
rows.notes: Port the terminate: false regression case from harness-tools.test.ts with the citation re-pin.

rows.change: registryReader(value, context) is a RegistryReader over a Chord v2 registry value whose composition is a registry snapshot: snapshot() reads the current composition and subscribe observes its compositions synchronously inside Chord's batch, so a Harness opened in a Chord object takes its extensions from a Chord registry.
rows.notes: Blocked on Chord v2 registries (chord@1.5.0/Added#3, group F), which phase 4 ports with the parts of Chord v2 durable needs (decision 0013, Durable). PiSharp's IRegistryReader (Harness/Types.cs) and Registry.cs need no other change.

rows.change: Unlisted: pi-durable's test suite changes with the 1.4.0 and 1.5.0 API changes. 68 upstream test files that PiSharp's durable tests cite changed in the range.
rows.notes: PiSharp's durable tests port upstream's cases and cite them (see the durable area of sync-1.5.0-worklist.json). Each durable row ports its upstream cases with it; this row tracks the cited test files no other row names, so the re-sync re-pins every durable test citation.

rows.change: `RemoteWatcher` implements Durable's v1.5.0 `FileWatcher`: `close(context)` is `stop(context)`, and it delivers tagged `FileChange`s (`{ kind: "paths", paths }`, `{ kind: "overflow" }`, `{ kind: "failed", error }`) instead of `WatchChange` objects; a failure stops it. The daemon's `watch` protocol is unchanged: the wire still says `{ overflow: true }` or `{ paths }`.
rows.notes: PiSharp has the v1.2.0 shapes in Durable: IFileWatcher with CloseAsync and the WatchChange records (FileSystem.cs:126 and :154-160). The rename to stop and FileChange is Durable's change (group E, phase 4); this row follows it in the remote client, which PiSharp does not have yet (env.remote-execution-env).

rows.change: When the daemon cannot start a helper thread for `exec` or `pty` (for example at a cgroup task limit), the request fails with `spawn_error` instead of hanging, and the command already started is killed and reaped (#11433).
rows.notes: Daemon side. It comes with the daemon either way the owner decides (env.daemon).

rows.change: On Unix the daemon blocks `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` and `SIGHUP` before it starts any thread and waits for them on a thread of its own, which kills every process group it started and exits, so `Connection.close()` (which ends stdin and sends `SIGTERM`) no longer leaves commands running. On Windows a job object kills each command's own process with the daemon but not the processes it started; the protocol doc now says so.
rows.notes: A C# daemon would register the same signals with PosixSignalRegistration. It comes with upstream's binaries if the owner runs them (env.daemon).

rows.change: Unlisted (#10716, 479d6e5e2): when the daemon exits or fails before `hello`, the startup error adds the last 20 lines (at most 2,000 characters) of its stderr, with terminal escapes and control characters removed, because a tool error can reach the model. A ready session fails as soon as the daemon exits, even while a process it started keeps a pipe open.
rows.notes: In no changelog. Part of the client (env.remote-execution-env).

rows.change: Unlisted (#11605, 102d12871): a watch `change` event whose path list would not fit in a 16 MiB frame is sent as the existing `{ overflow: true }` event. Before, `write_frame` refused it and the daemon's only output writer stopped, so requests hung until the client's 30 s silence limit dropped the connection.
rows.notes: In no changelog. Daemon side (env.daemon).

rows.change: `RemoteExecutionEnv` is a Durable `ExecutionEnv` whose file operations, commands, line scans, `listFiles` and watches run on a pi-env daemon through a `Connection`: frames over the daemon's stdin and stdout, pings every 5 s, a 30 s silence limit, and a new daemon at the next request after a loss (requests of the lost one fail with `lost: true`). Results match `NodeExecutionEnv` on that machine; only error messages differ. `LocalExecutionEnv` is the local environment plus `listFiles` through a daemon on the same machine, and `nodePlatform(info)` maps the daemon's platform names to Node's.
rows.notes: PiSharp implements Durable's ExecutionEnv locally (IExecutionEnv, Shell.cs:150; LocalExecutionEnv.cs:43) and lists files in process with the daemon's semantics (LocalFileListing.cs:30), so local listing needs no daemon. The remote client is missing. It builds on Durable's v1.5.0 ExecutionEnv (phase 4), and pi-env depends on pi-durable and Chord. The coding agent does not use pi-env (not in coding-agent's v1.5.0 dependencies, no imports in its src), so nothing pulls it into phase 2.

rows.change: `connectSsh(target)` detects the remote system, deploys the daemon the package ships for it (named by its SHA-256 and verified before every start) and connects; `sshConnection` does the same lazily at the first operation. `ssh` runs with BatchMode, strict host-key checking against the application's own known-hosts file under a fixed alias, and no forwarding, shared connections or configured commands; `scanHostKey`, `acceptHostKey` and `forgetHostKey` manage trusted keys, and a changed key is never accepted without removing the old one. Windows targets are detected and deployed through PowerShell.
rows.notes: Security-sensitive: the host-key flow puts a fingerprint in front of the owner to compare out of band. Which binaries get deployed follows env.daemon. The daemon's `--token` argument is a stdout sync marker, not a credential; check it against the rule that secrets never reach command lines.

rows.change: `openTerminal(connection, options)` runs a program, by default the login shell, in a daemon pseudo-terminal: raw output, input in arrival order, resizing (`SIGWINCH`), the exit code, and `foreground()` naming the process group in front when it is not the program's own. `localDaemon()` starts the daemon for this machine, for terminals without SSH. Unix only; Windows answers `ENOTSUP`.

`pi-env serve --token <hex>`, a Rust program, prints `PI-ENV <token>` and then speaks big-endian length-prefixed frames (request, result, error, event, cancel, ping; a JSON object plus a raw payload, at most 16 MiB) on stdin and stdout. File operations run on a worker pool and `exec`, `pty` and `watch` on threads of their own, with output windows, cancellation by request id, replies ahead of bulk output, native watching with polling on Windows and network file systems, and a kill of every process group on silence or end of input.
rows.notes: Decision 0013: port it or run upstream's binaries, settled when phase 5 starts. Porting means a C# NativeAOT daemon for Linux, macOS, Android (Termux) and Windows on x64 and arm64. Running means shipping upstream's per-platform binaries from the npm package's bin/ and verifying their SHA-256.

rows.change: The tests run Durable's env conformance suite against `RemoteExecutionEnv` over a daemon pipe, compare random operation sequences and Durable's tools against `NodeExecutionEnv` on the same machine, check that old daemons answer `not_supported`, and run the suite over a real SSH server when `PI_ENV_SSH_HOST` is set.
rows.notes: PiSharp's port of Durable's env conformance kit (EnvConformance.cs) can be reused. Tests stay offline: the external SSH suite stays opt-in, behind its environment variable.

rows.change: Chord now owns the one watch API Durable used to define: `Watchable<T>` (`value`, `watch(context)`), `WatchHandle<T>` (`value`, `start(listener)`, `stop()`, `closed`) and its implementation `Watch<T>`, which a source feeds with `advance(call, context)`, `fail(error, context)`, `end(end)` and `endAfterDelivery()`. Listeners get a tagged `WatchCall<T>` (`{ kind: "value", value, ops, retired }` or `{ kind: "failed", error }`) and the context; frames that arrive while the listener runs fold into one call through `PendingOps` (past 10,000 ops one `[["r", newest]]`), a failure keeps the watch open, and a retirement is a flag on the next value call, not an end. `WatchEnd` is tagged by `kind` (`stopped`, `aborted`, `ended`, `listener_error`, `failed`), with `abort()` and `observeAbort(signal)` in place of `cancel()` and `observeCancellation(signal)`.
rows.notes: PiSharp has Durable v1.2.0's watch: `IWatchHandle<T>` with a `(value, ops, ctx)` listener where null retires the watch, and `WatchEnd`/`WatchEndReason` (stopped, cancelled, session_closed, retired, listener_error, session_failed) in TypesSession.cs:161-232, implemented by `CommittedWatch<T>` (Session/Observation.cs:222). Missing: the generic `Watch<T>` a source drives, tagged calls, failure calls, retirement as a flag, `endAfterDelivery()` and folding through PendingOps (chord.delta-pending-ops). Needed by phase 4: pi-durable v1.5.0 imports Watch, WatchCall, WatchEnd and WatchHandle from Chord (durable@1.5.0/Breaking Changes#5, #19 and Changed#1, group E). The owner decides whether this shared code moves into phase 4 (release 1.5.0) and whether it lives in a new PiSharp.Chord project or stays in PiSharp.Durable/Chord.
rows.deferred: Chord's watch API (IWatchHandle, IWatchable, WatchEnd by kind, tagged calls, Watch<T>) is ported in src/PiSharp.Durable/Chord/Watch.cs, but Durable's own watches (TypesSession.cs WatchEnd/WatchEndReason/IWatchHandle, Session/Observation.cs CommittedWatch) still follow v1.2.0: the coordinator assigned moving them onto Chord's to work list area watches (row durable.watch-handles). packages/chord/README.md has no PiSharp counterpart; chord/src/index.ts is the barrel, with no C# counterpart.

rows.change: `NativeWatchable<T>` is an in-process value that changes and can be watched; its `NativeWatchHandle<T>`, implemented by `NativeWatch<T>`, has the lifecycle of `Watch` without ops: one `NativeWatchCall<T>` (`{ kind: "value", value }` or `{ kind: "failed", error }`) per value in order, and past 100 pending values one call with the value of the optional `replace()` or the newest value. It ends with the same tagged `WatchEnd`.
rows.notes: PiSharp has no native watch. Durable v1.5.0 re-exports `NativeWatchCall` for its synchronous observers (durable@1.5.0/Breaking Changes#19, group E), and Chord v2's writables, registry values and `ref.state` are native watchables (chord.next-documents-state, chord.next-registries). Shares the lifecycle code of chord.watch-handle.

rows.change: `PendingOps` keeps the pending ops of one slow consumer raw and folds them while they wait: appends to one path join, a primitive set replaces earlier leaf ops on its path, and `r` drops everything before it. `size` counts the ops after folding; `take()` empties the queue and returns a `PendingTake` with the folded ops, or a `replace` past 10,000 ops. Received batches and op tuples are never mutated.
rows.notes: PiSharp's delta port has the op types (Ops.cs) and no folding queue; the new class goes next to them. `Watch` folds with it (chord.watch-handle), and pi-durable v1.5.0 imports it from chord/delta, so phase 4 needs it.

Descriptions are hashed into fingerprints, `coverage` checks that a provider covers a consumer (equal placements, agreeing arguments) and `accepts` adapters serve old consumers. A reference is `Ref<C>`, a factory returns `ImplementationOf<C>`, and failures are `ChordError`s with the codes of the guide.
rows.notes: PiSharp has no Chord kernel: decision 0005 ported only what pi-durable imported. A fingerprint is hash64 of the description's canonical JSON, so a C# host can serve TypeScript peers (browsers, Node hosts) only if it reproduces both byte for byte; pin fingerprints of upstream's test contracts. The 1.3.0 renames (Ref, ImplementationOf, variant) are naming for a fresh port. TypeScript-only checks (PlacementFor, the hostFamily field) become generic constraints or run-time checks. The coding agent does not use Chord: coding-agent's v1.5.0 package.json does not list it (coding-agent@1.2.0 removed the dependency), its src imports nothing from it, and examples/tsconfig.json only repeats the root path map, so nothing pulls Chord into phase 2. An `invalid` error's message is `<path> <message>` in pi-schema's words and its `details` are pi-schema `ValidationError`s (`{ path, keyword, message }`); link frames, descriptions, fingerprints and identities stay the same for schemas with the same JSON.
