rows.change: `host.serve(type, factory, options)` serves a type. `lifetime: "referenced"` (the default) creates an object at the first `get` of its address and disposes it after its last reference is released, plus `linger`; `lifetime: "host"` keeps the type's one object from facet load to host close, for local types whose input accepts `{}` and without `linger`, and only such objects may register. Factories declare by name: `self.state(name, schema, initial or { init }, { version, migrate })` cells with per-cell versions (`init(ctx)` runs before the object goes live), `self.resource(name, { version, deps, exclusive, open, close })`, `self.on(name, source, [select,] handler)`, and unnamed `self.derive` and `self.task`; a repeated name is `invalid/duplicate`.
rows.notes: TypeScript-only parts (ServeOptionsFor and the compile-time refusal of lifetime host, the EventOf, ValueOf, StateOptions and Lifetime types) become C# overloads or generic constraints over the same run-time refusals.

rows.change:
`createHost

({ name, self, principalKey, upstream, ... })` hosts objects for the app's principal type: `self` is the principal of the host's own code, `connect(link, { principal })` names what the parent's requests act as, and principals are recognized by `principalKey`; Chord invents none. `defineFacet` facets get a `FacetApi` (`serve`, `name`, `root`, `registry` and `signal`, which aborts once that run of the facet is no longer installed), `host.load` installs facets with host-lifetime objects live first (`awaitHostObjects`), and `host.root(fn)` runs code outside objects with a `ctx`.
rows.notes: The principal type parameter maps to C# generics; FacetApi.signal maps to a CancellationToken.

rows.change: An awaited reference has its state: `ctx.get` and `host.get` resolve once the reference is live and every state member of its variant has a first snapshot, and reject with the activation error, `aborted` or `unavailable/ready_timeout` after `readyTimeout` (60 s); `host.hold` is the synchronous form and `self.get` stays synchronous, its object going live only once its references are hydrated. State members are typed `T` (read early: `not_ready`; outside the variant: `not_in_variant`), a held remote reference stays subscribed (`state: false` makes a method-only reference), references to one object share one binding per host and key, kept hydrated after release by `HostOptions.linger`, and a remote call refuses a ctx from another host (`invalid/foreign_ctx`).
rows.notes: Remote references are unions discriminated by variant in TypeScript; C# needs a variant switch over typed members.

rows.change: Hosts exchange JSON frames, declared once as the schema that validates them. Links announce `PROTOCOL_VERSION` (4) in `hello`; peers of another version, or none, are refused: the link closes with `protocol-version <n>` and both sides report `onProtocolMismatch`. In protocol 4 a `hold` implies its variant's state (`state: false` until `sub`), the provider answers with a `shape` (with `variant`, without `codeVersion`) and snapshots, `state` frames are addressed by hold and member with `as: snap | reset | ops | error`, `resync` asks for a member again, `again` marks a re-hold after a link loss, `origin` names the client connection, remote tokens carry `host`, a hold's input is normalized, and void or argument-less calls omit `args` and `value`.
rows.notes: The frame schema is the interop surface with TypeScript Chord peers (browser tabs, Node hosts). Test frames against upstream's link tests; authored expectations are never labelled as captures (0013).

rows.change: Links are `memoryLinkPair()`, `ipcLink` over a Node IPC channel, and `webSocketLink` with `acceptWebSockets` on a server; connections ping, and a dead link releases everything held through it. A failed IPC write (the `EPIPE` of a write to a peer that just exited) ends the link with `ipc send failed: EPIPE` instead of an unhandled error that crashes the process.
rows.notes: Node IPC channels have no .NET counterpart: a C# ipcLink needs framing over a child's stdio or a pipe, and a link to a Node child host needs Node's IPC serialization. WebSockets map to System.Net.WebSockets. Standing rule: servers bind to 127.0.0.1.

rows.change: Peers acknowledge what they processed (`ack` frames, announced with `acks` in `hello`). While a window of frames (`LinkOptions.window`, 256 KiB) is unacknowledged, state frames wait at the sender, coalesced per subscription; calls, results, control frames and the first unit of a new reference are never held back, units for reloads and re-holds are built lazily, and waiting ops are capped per link (`pendingCap`, four windows), beyond which the oldest streams become resets. `Link.send` returns the encoded size, so only links that report it are windowed, and `AcceptOptions.maxCalls` answers calls beyond the limit with `unavailable/too_many_calls`.
rows.notes: Under load a result can arrive before the state change it caused; the port keeps that order rule, and the tests check it.

rows.change: Call arguments, results and state snapshots whose JSON exceeds `PACK_THRESHOLD` (64K characters) are deflated (raw deflate, level 1): over IPC as a base64 field, over WebSockets as a binary message. Relays forward the deflated bytes unread and only the host that uses the payload inflates it; `webSocketLink(socket, { compress, acceptPacked })` controls sending and accepting packed frames, and `inflateMessage` turns a packed message back into a text frame.
rows.notes: System.IO.Compression.DeflateStream writes raw deflate, matching `zlib.deflateRawSync`. Servers should refuse packed frames from untrusted clients (acceptPacked false), which bounds decompression bombs.

rows.change: A server relays between its children and from clients to workers: `host.route(prefix, { authorize, resolve, principal })` reaches addressable hosts (a worker spawned on demand), a forwarded principal is accepted only from the parent link, a relay refuses a hold whose target disagrees with its contract's placement, and a client's hold carries an opaque `origin` (the accepting host's id for that connection) that relays forward, so a disconnect releases exactly that client's holds. A host a route resolves is admitted even when the reference that asked for it is released, its client disconnects or its principal is revoked meanwhile, and a link already closed when accepted or routed to is never kept as a connection.
rows.notes: The 1.5.0 fix stops a spawned worker's lifetime-host references to its parent from waiting into `unavailable/ready_timeout`; the 1.3.0 fix stops a dead route link from failing every later call with `unavailable` and leaking its ping timer. Both need tests.

rows.change: `host.reload(facets)` swaps code while it runs: work in flight finishes on its code version (`codeVersion`, formerly epoch), state is kept and a cell whose version rose migrates at a safe point, derivations are recomputed at the commit, and listeners on replaced state subscribe again. A reload starts an object's new tasks only after its aborted ones finished (at most `taskStopDeadline`, 5 s); a forced retirement of a code version first aborts the roots still on it (`superseded`, up to 1 s), relayed calls follow their root's signal, and a resource kept across a reload adopts the newest declaration's `close`.
rows.notes: Hot reload of C# code means collectible AssemblyLoadContexts, one per code version; how facets are built and loaded is the owner's decision (chord.host-manager, chord.next-plugins). Retention is chord.kernel-retention.

rows.change: A parent coordinates a reload's prepare and commit across its child hosts. A child whose hello arrives while a cluster reload runs is synced or reconciled when the reload ends (one already behind is fenced at once, so its roots' calls up are admitted), the coordinator retires before it sends `prepare`, a child waits for its parent's `retire` (at most `retireDeadline`), and a child coming in step learns which code versions the parent retired.
rows.notes: Before these fixes a late child stayed on the old code and failed every call `superseded`, and parents' old roots got `superseded` on children that retired early.

rows.change: Disposed objects leave the host at once (before, one per distinct guest, session or input stayed reachable until its address was used again); references no longer keep every code version's services, and with them old factory code, reachable; call, task and root contexts detach from long-lived signals when they close instead of staying linked through `AbortSignal.any`; and a resource kept across a reload stops holding the code of the run that first opened it.
rows.notes: The .NET equivalents: old code versions as collectible AssemblyLoadContexts, which unload only when nothing references their types, and linked CancellationTokenSources that must be disposed when a context closes. Needs unload tests (a WeakReference to the load context).

rows.change: Hosts, facets, objects, natives and references: activation with failure causes, backoff and parked attempts that wake on change, principals and variants, links to children, a parent and routes to addressable hosts (`host.route` returns a `RouteHandle` with `retry` and `suspend`, and a failed `resolve` fails its holders `waiting` with no backoff timer), revocation, cycle checks across hosts, presence and keep-alive counts. Slice 8 adds `self.retryOn(...sources)`, wake signals and root scopes (`host.root(fn, context, { principal })`, sealed when `fn` settles, `context` aborts or the host closes; anonymous with `principal: undefined`), and `self.follow` takes another runtime's synchronous observers as sources.
rows.notes: The largest v2 layer (8,815 lines). `self.follow` is how Chord follows Durable's views (durable@1.5.0/Added#3, group E).

rows.change: `host.load` and `host.reload` work per plugin: a plugin whose setup, factory or declarations fail is left out at `load` (`{ failed }`) or kept on its old code at `reload` (`failed` in the report; `reload(facets, ctx, { failed })` for build and evaluation failures), a closure rule keeps a consumer old when its provider was kept old, and an abort after the commit rejects with `details.committed`. A reload stages, commits atomically or rolls back, swaps pure members, restarts natives, and carries holds, `accepts`, jobs and registries across.
rows.notes: Same code-loading question as chord.reload: collectible AssemblyLoadContexts per code version.

rows.change: Routines (`self.on`, `self.onLive`, `sleep`) and jobs (`defineJob`, `self.job`): owned work a call starts that outlives the call, as intent (a transaction), run (any effect) and finish (a transaction on the current code), with dedupe, `busy` and `running`. Persisted jobs (`persist: { resume }`) resume after a restart, with a stored `abort(id, ctx)` and deferred state changes.
rows.notes: Persisted jobs need chord.next-store.

rows.change: Links: one `Message` type checked after every decode (skipped on trusted links), text and binary codecs, opaque parts with size limits and compression at the origin, the handshake and heartbeat, and IPC and WebSocket transports. Remote: a `HostLink` per link with a provider side per origin and one consumer side, holds, relayed holds and calls, replicas, and the ack-clocked window per origin with a call window; a link reads `origin` only on parent and route links (a protocol error on a child link) and drops a per-origin record once it is idle.
rows.notes: v2's protocol is not v1's (chord.wire-protocol); the two share no frames. Same transport questions as chord.links-transports.

rows.change: One store per host over a backend (SQLite through chord/sqlite, or Durable Objects' storage): declared tables, queries compiled once to SQL, writes, one commit queue, an outbox, the documents engine, eager table migrations, export and import (archives that carry document revisions) and batch apply. 1.5.0 adds one id allocator for every id, claims per table and per document namespace, Durable's semantics for a refused commit (it rejects only that commit; an unknown outcome stops the store), and `ChordStore.commitSeries(commits, receive, ctx)`: several commits in one backend transaction, each at its own seq with its own outbox row and check, replacing `commitInBatch`.
rows.notes: Needed by phase 4: Durable's StoreStorage (durable@1.5.0/Added#1, group E) keeps a Session's records as store tables and stores each Session commit call through commitSeries, so StoreStorage cannot be ported without this row. 6,083 lines. The SQLite backend uses chord.sqlite and chord.sqlite-run-counted; the Durable Objects backend follows chord.sqlite-cloudflare.

rows.change: `defineRegistry<C, V>(name, { version })` tokens shared by plugins, served by the defining plugin's facet with `host.serve(R, { compose, accepts })`. Facets (`self.contribute(R, value)`) and host-lifetime objects contribute plain values or watchables, kept in a table sorted by plugin name and composed lazily; readers use `self.registry(R)`, a declared dependency that fails `transient` with `unavailable/undeclared` when nobody serves it, or `host.registry(R, ctx)`, a `RegistryValue<V>` with `observe(observer, ctx)`. `accepts` adapts older contributions and readers; helpers `keyedEntries` and `orderedEntries`; `onError` kinds `registry_conflict`, `registry_failed`, `contribution_failed` and `contribution_refused`.
rows.notes: Durable's registryReader reads a RegistryValue (durable@1.5.0/Added#15, group E), so phase 4 needs at least the RegistryValue shape. Not v1's registries (chord.registries-v1).

rows.change: The Node plugins component finds plugin directories, builds each facet with esbuild (an optional peer dependency) and evaluates it with `vm.Script`, maps plugin stack traces (`mapStack`), installs plugin dependencies, watches plugin and base code, and rolls reloads out across hosts (`RolloutStep` returns `{ hosts }`). Slice 10 adds one definition per facet kind (`kinds: { name: { platform, hostPackages } }`, modules given at `plugins.load(host, { kind, core, modules })`), `createPluginRuntime()` without esbuild for workers, `scripts(kind)`, and cross-plugin imports by plugin name (`@app/notes/contract`).
rows.notes: Owner decision: this component builds and evaluates TypeScript. A C# port could compile C# plugins (Roslyn, collectible AssemblyLoadContexts) or run TypeScript plugins through the Node bridge; neither is upstream's code path. Installing plugin dependencies runs npm.

rows.change: A Web-standard `fetch` handler built from what plugins contribute to the registry `Http` (routes, wraps, sockets, allowed hosts, relays, CSP sources), with authenticators from the registry `Authenticators`, responses as descriptions (`json`, `html`, `bytes` with ranges, `redirect`, `error`, `fileResponse`) and a security baseline on by default: provenance by socket and `Host`, foreign requests anonymous, `Origin` checks, default headers with a per-response CSP nonce, signed cookies and safe downloads. Chord's own Node listener is a host-lifetime object, `nodeRequest` mounts the handler on an app's own server, and the links endpoint and plugin sockets have a heartbeat and close when their contribution leaves.
rows.notes: ASP.NET Core is the natural host (Kestrel plus a middleware for the handler). Standing rules: the listener binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, and secrets such as the cookie signing key never reach the browser or logs.

rows.change: `createWorkers(server, kind, options)` runs a forked worker process per address of one host kind, started on demand by the route it owns, stopped when idle and never restarted by itself (a failure stays until `retry` or a rollout); `workerMain` is the worker's side, and the server builds and ships the worker's plugins.
rows.notes: Forked Node processes with IPC upstream; the C# port uses child processes with a pipe link (chord.links-transports, chord.host-manager) and ships plugins as chord.next-plugins decides.

rows.change: pi-evals (private) holds behavioral evals of the coding agent, built on vitest-evals. Host evals (`eval:host` smoke, `eval:audit` documentation audit) run against a configured runtime; documentation-lift evals (`*.docs.eval.ts`) run each case in fresh `without_docs` and `with_docs` Docker containers built from the packed workspace, pair the arms, and report the lift. In the range upstream added a prompt-template documentation eval and dropped the autoevals dependency.
rows.notes: Decision 0013 ports it as a repository tool, with no package. The evals call a real provider (`PI_PROVIDER`, `PI_MODEL`), so they stay out of the automated suite (standing rule: tests stay faux and offline) and run only on demand. The documentation-lift evals measure Pi's docs; for PiSharp they would measure PiSharp's docs and website. Phase 7 decides which suites apply.
